name: Up an exchange — rook against minor piece

plans.label: Rook on the seventh or on an open file
plans.description: The extra exchange converts through activity, not arithmetic: get the rook to the seventh rank or onto a fully open file before cashing anything in.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'The rook earns the exchange first', whose success was rook activity in general. It is now the two placements the phrase concretely means: the rook stands on the seventh rank, or on a fully open file. A rook can be active in ways this misses, and inactive on an open file that leads nowhere. Original success note: 'Rook activity quality is not rules arithmetic.' Degenerate-case guard: the earlier draft of this signature was vacuously true over an empty piece set, so an existence clause was added. On a pawnless board every file is open, so the open-file arms fired for free; at least one pawn must exist.

plans.label: A passer on one wing, pawns still on the other
plans.description: Create a second front: a passed pawn on one wing while pawns still stand on the other, so the minor piece must commute and the defending king can hold only one side.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Stretch the defence across two wings', whose success was wing counts and switching distance. It is now the two-front position itself: a White passed pawn on one wing and White pawns still standing on the other. How fast the rook switches between them is not measured. Original success note: 'Wing counts and switching distance are outside this vocabulary.'

plans.label: Give the exchange back into a pawn ending
plans.description: The cleanest conversion is often returning the rook for the minor piece and a pawn, reaching a pure pawn ending a pawn to the good. Pricing that ending is still the player's job.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Give the exchange back to win', whose success was whether the pawn ending wins. It is now the ending it steers into: no rooks and no Black minor piece remain, and White is at least a pawn up. Whether that ending wins is left where the plan left it — uncounted. Original success note: 'Whether the resulting pawn ending wins is not expressed by this vocabulary.'

plans.label: Fortress on one wing
plans.description: Pawns on one wing, the minor piece anchored on a protected square, the king guarding the entry squares: if the rook has no entry point and no pawn to attack twice, the exchange means nothing.

success.note: A fortress is an outcome, not a census; no structural signature is honest here.

plans.label: Move no pawn without a reason
plans.description: Every pawn move creates a square or a target the rook can work against; keep the pawns where the minor piece and king defend them, and make the rook prove it can enter before conceding anything.

success.note: Weakness creation is a judgment the feature set cannot make.

watch: Pawn counts are outside the vocabulary: this fires whether the exchange is clean or fully compensated by pawns — count the pawns before trusting the label 'up'.
Entry squares for the rook and king are the real question of this family and are not expressible; the trigger names the material census only.
Colour convention: White is authored as the rook side. Mirror when reversed; the trigger fires only for this orientation.
typicalMistakes: Keeping the rook when returning the exchange won on the spot — the material habit outliving the position.
Grabbing a poisoned pawn and letting the fortress set up while the rook is away.
As the defender, advancing a fortress pawn onto a square the rook attacks sideways — a fortress pawn that moves stops being a fortress pawn.
Trading pawns as the rook side: each pawn pair that leaves the board moves the position toward the drawn bare-minor ending.

sources: Family per design/04-content-architecture.md section 4 (practical conversion: up-an-exchange; rook + minor called 'the practical nightmare band').
Tablebase honesty: typical positions of this family exceed seven pieces; no tablebase ground truth exists for them and none was consulted.
UNGROUNDED: plan, watch, and mistake prose is authored endgame-literature consensus rendered by the author; no engine or tablebase has graded any claim in this entry.

Trigger gap: the census requires White's only piece to be the rook and Black's to be one minor; rook-and-minor versus rook-and-minor exchange-up positions, and pawn compensation, are not expressible and are recorded here.

D44 orphan status, re-measured 2026-08-16 with `make expression-census` over 827 authored spine positions across 56 packs (the 2026-08-15 reading of this line said 694 positions and is superseded; the substance is unchanged): no pack under content/drafts references this entry and its trigger still fires on 0 of the 827, so every signature here is verified only against constructed witnesses. It stands alone deliberately - the trigger-gap note above already records that the census is narrower than the family, and no authored pack plays an exchange-up conversion.
